text:
B: Hiya, hello! Can you hear me alright?
A: Hi! Yeah, I can. Sorry, my internet's been a bit funny today. I'm Megan.
B: I'm Gemma. Erm, I have to tell you, I think we've got something in common. Jade said your guinea pig's called Biscuit?
A: Oh my god, yeah! Is that your dog? Jade said there was another Biscuit but I thought she'd got muddled.
B: No, she's right. Biscuit the greyhound. She's thirteen, and she's on the sofa behind me now, if you can see her ears.
A: I can! Aw, she's gorgeous. I love greyhounds. They just look so gentle, do you know what I mean?
B: She is. She's frightened of absolutely everything, but she's gentle. Why Biscuit for yours?
A: Erm, he's kind of a light brown, like a digestive. And when we got him from the rescue he wouldn't stop eating, so. My boyfriend picked it, really.
B: Ha, ours came with the name, from the rescue. We didn't want to confuse her at her age.
A: That's sweet. Erm, sorry, what do you do? I should've asked.
B: Don't be sorry. I'm a pharmacy technician at a hospital in Nottingham. I do the medicines on two wards, so when someone comes in, I check what they were taking at home matches what's been written up. You'd be surprised how often it doesn't. Somebody's on the wrong dose, or a tablet's been missed off completely. It's sort of my job to catch it before it gets to them. And I look after a few junior techs.
A: That sounds really important. Like, really stressful.
B: It can be. I do lie awake sometimes going over things, if I'm honest. But I like it. What about you? Jade mentioned birds?
A: Yeah, I'm at uni, second year, wildlife and conservation. So lots of fieldwork, which I love, and then writing up, which I don't. The stats bit, I just kind of freeze, and I'm always up till midnight the night before a deadline.
B: Oh, I was exactly the same with stats. I started a degree, actually, biomedical science, and I left after the first year. I just didn't get on with it.
A: Oh really? Do you, erm, sorry, do you regret it?
B: Sometimes, a bit. But I'd not be doing this if I'd stayed, and I'm good at this. So, you know. Stick with yours, though, it sounds like you love it.
A: I do. I just worry about getting a job at the end. I want to be a ranger, or do education stuff with kids, for a wildlife trust or the RSPB.
B: You'd be brilliant with kids, I can tell. You've got that sort of patient voice.
A: Aw, thank you. My nan's got an allotment, and I used to help her when I was li'le, and that's kind of why I got into it all.
B: That's lovely. I do tomatoes and sweet peas, that's my limit. My tomatoes were rubbish this year, though.
A: Were they? Did they get blight? My nan's did.
B: I think so, the leaves went all brown. Sorry, I'm keeping you talking about tomatoes.
A: No, I love this. Honestly, it's the best bit.
B: Do you get out much near you, nature-wise?
A: Mersea Island, when we can. And the Suffolk coast. That's like my treat day. Do you walk Biscuit somewhere nice?
B: The canal, every day. There's a heron that stands in the same spot every morning. Biscuit's terrified of it.
A: Ha! Herons are terrifying, to be fair, they're like dinosaurs.
B: That's exactly what Rob says. Oh, I think we're nearly out of time.
A: Aw. Give Biscuit a stroke from me.
B: I will, and you give yours a bit of carrot.
